title: UAE Cabinet meeting, 23 April 2026: agentic AI across 50% of government within two years

excerpts.text: Mohammed bin Rashid unveils framework to deploy agentic AI across 50% of government sectors within 2 years
excerpts.where: UAE Cabinet release, Government Media Office, 23 April 2026, headline

excerpts.text: this transformation’s defined timeline is two years. During that period, the performance of ministers, directors general, and entities will be assessed based on their ability to adopt this transformation
excerpts.where: UAE Cabinet release, Government Media Office, 23 April 2026, timeline and assessment

excerpts.text: This project aims to transform 50% of government sectors, services, and operations to implement autonomous Agentic AI models within two years
excerpts.where: UAE Cabinet release, Government Media Office, 23 April 2026, project aim

excerpts.text: Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed will oversee the implementation of the UAE President’s vision of this major governmental transformation. We have formed a dedicated taskforce, chaired by Mohammad Al Gergawi, to drive execution.
excerpts.where: UAE Cabinet release, Government Media Office, 23 April 2026, oversight and taskforce

excerpts.text: The Cabinet further approved a “government services data sharing policy” based on the principle of collecting data once and using it securely across entities
excerpts.where: UAE Cabinet release, Government Media Office, 23 April 2026, data sharing policy

excerpts.text: The project includes a phased implementation across ministries and federal entities, based on continuous performance and impact assessment.
excerpts.where: UAE Cabinet release, Government Media Office, 23 April 2026, phased implementation

excerpts.text: People come first.
excerpts.where: UAE Cabinet release, Government Media Office, 23 April 2026, principle

title: National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence

excerpts.text: The National Artificial Intelligence Security Policy defines minimum security requirements for adoption of AI in the UAE. It establishes governance, infrastructure, algorithm protection, operational safety, threat monitoring, and performance evaluation to manage emerging AI risks.
excerpts.where: UAE Cyber Security Council, National Cyber Security Policy for AI, u.ae page, overview

excerpts.text: Adversarial AI Attacks Requirements to understand and anticipate potential AI/ML attacks, fostering a proactive security approach that includes education, awareness, and comprehensive defense techniques, continuous monitoring, testing, and robust incident response.
excerpts.where: UAE Cyber Security Council, National Cyber Security Policy for AI, u.ae page, adversarial AI attacks

excerpts.text: AI Monitoring & Response Requirements to establish an effective AI/ML security analytics framework for real-time threat detection and predictive insights.
excerpts.where: UAE Cyber Security Council, National Cyber Security Policy for AI, u.ae page, AI monitoring and response

excerpts.text: Operational Safety Requirements to tailor security measures based on the distinct applications of AI/ML systems, ensuring human oversight in critical decision-making
excerpts.where: UAE Cyber Security Council, National Cyber Security Policy for AI, u.ae page, operational safety

excerpts.text: Governance Requirements to establish a robust governance framework for AI/ML systems, ensuring their secure design, development, and operation
excerpts.where: UAE Cyber Security Council, National Cyber Security Policy for AI, u.ae page, governance

title: Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL): short excerpts only

excerpts.text: Any data related to a specific natural person or related to a natural person that can be identified directly or indirectly by linking the data, through the use of identification elements such as his/her name, voice, image, identification number
excerpts.where: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL), official English text, Article 1 (Definitions), Personal Data

excerpts.text: An establishment or natural person that has Personal Data, and by virtue of its activity, determines whether individually or jointly with other persons or establishments, the method and criteria for processing such Personal Data and the purpose of processing it
excerpts.where: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL), official English text, Article 1 (Definitions), Controller

excerpts.text: Provisions of this Decree by Law shall not apply to the following: a. Government Data b. Governmental entities which control or process Personal Data.
excerpts.where: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL), official English text, Article 2 (Scope), exclusions

excerpts.text: It is prohibited to process Personal Data without the consent of its owner. The following cases shall be excluded from such prohibition: 1. If the processing is necessary to protect public interest.
excerpts.where: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL), official English text, Article 4 (Processing without consent)

excerpts.text: Processing shall be carried out in a fair, transparent and lawful manner. 2. Personal Data shall be collected for a specific and clear purpose. It shall not be processed at any later time in a manner incompatible with such purpose.
excerpts.where: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL), official English text, Article 5 (Processing controls)

excerpts.text: The Consent shall be prepared in a clear, simple, unambiguous and easily accessible manner, whether in writing or electronically. c. The Consent shall include the Data Subject's right to withdraw it easily.
excerpts.where: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL), official English text, Article 6 (Consent)

excerpts.text: Maintain a special record for Personal Data, provided that such record shall include the data of both the Controller and the Data Protection Officer, a description of the categories of Personal Data
excerpts.where: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL), official English text, Article 7 (Controller obligations), record

excerpts.text: the Controller shall, at the time it becomes aware of the existence of any breach or violation of Personal Data of the Data Subject that would prejudice the privacy, confidentiality and security of data, notify the Bureau of such breach
excerpts.where: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL), official English text, Article 9 (Breach reporting)

excerpts.text: The Data Subject shall have the right to request the correction of his/her inaccurate Personal data, or request to complete the data held by the Controller without undue delay
excerpts.where: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL), official English text, Article 15 (Correction)

excerpts.text: the right to request erasure of his/ her Personal Data held by the Controller in any of the following cases: a. His/her Personal Data is no longer necessary for the purposes for which it is collected or processed.
excerpts.where: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL), official English text, Article 15 (Erasure)

excerpts.text: The Data Subject shall have the right to object to any decisions resulting from automated processing, including profiling, particularly those decisions which have legal impact on or adversely affect the Data Subject.
excerpts.where: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL), official English text, Article 18 (Automated processing), objection

excerpts.text: The Controller shall include the human element in reviewing automated processing decisions at the request of the Data Subject.
excerpts.where: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL), official English text, Article 18 (Automated processing), human review

excerpts.text: the Controller shall, before carrying out the processing, evaluate the impact of the proposed processing operations on the protection of Personal Data, when using any of the modern technologies that would pose a high risk
excerpts.where: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL), official English text, Article 21 (Impact assessment)

excerpts.text: Personal Data may be transferred to outside of the State in the following cases approved by the Bureau: 1. The State or Province to which the Personal Data is transferred shall have legislations addressing Personal Data Protection.
excerpts.where: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL), official English text, Article 22 (Cross-border transfer)

excerpts.text: The Data Subject shall have the right to submit complaints to the Bureau if he/she believes that there is a violation of this Decree by Law
excerpts.where: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL), official English text, Article 24 (Complaints)

excerpts.text: The Council of Ministers, based upon a suggestion from the General Director of the Bureau, shall issue a decision to limit the actions which constitute a violation of this Decree by Law and its Executive Regulations, including administrative penalties
excerpts.where: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL), official English text, Article 26 (Administrative penalties)

title: Singapore launches Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI (law firm summary)

excerpts.text: On 22 January 2026, Singapore’s Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) launched the Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI (MGF) at the World Economic Forum 2026.
excerpts.where: Baker McKenzie, Singapore: Governance Framework for Agentic AI Launched, 29 January 2026, launch

excerpts.text: four core dimensions: (1) assessing and bounding the risks upfront, (2) making humans meaningfully accountable, (3) implementing technical controls and processes, and (4) enabling end-user responsibility.
excerpts.where: Baker McKenzie, Singapore: Governance Framework for Agentic AI Launched, 29 January 2026, four dimensions

excerpts.text: 2. Make humans meaningfully accountable A key innovation of the framework focuses on meaningful human accountability.
excerpts.where: Baker McKenzie, Singapore: Governance Framework for Agentic AI Launched, 29 January 2026, dimension 2

excerpts.text: The framework also requires human oversight mechanisms that can effectively override, intercept or review agentic AI actions. This is especially pivotal for actions that may have real-world material impact.
excerpts.where: Baker McKenzie, Singapore: Governance Framework for Agentic AI Launched, 29 January 2026, human oversight

excerpts.text: The framework suggests bounding risks by design by limiting what agents can do through controlling their tool access, permissions, operational environments and the scope of actions they may take.
excerpts.where: Baker McKenzie, Singapore: Governance Framework for Agentic AI Launched, 29 January 2026, bounding risks

excerpts.text: Enforce least-privilege access to tools and data to limit the agent’s impact on the external environment.
excerpts.where: Baker McKenzie, Singapore: Governance Framework for Agentic AI Launched, 29 January 2026, least privilege
